2_Introduction: The best performance, which showed 19.5454% certificated efficiency with a VOC of 1.096 V, a JSC of 25.503 mA/cm², and a FF of 69.9301%. Then, perovskite precursor solution (1.55 mol/L) was prepared at the stoichiometric ratio of Cs0.05MA0.05FA0.9PbI3.0. The perovskite film was deposited by spin-coating at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 40 s. During the spin-coating process, 160 µL of CB was dropped on the perovskite at 10 s, prior to the end of the second procedure. The samples were subsequently annealed on a hotplate at 120 °C for 13 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₀₅FA₀.₉PbI₃, leverages the synergistic A-site cation engineering—where the small ionic radii of Cs⁺ and MA⁺ enhance phase stability and suppress δ-phase formation while FA⁺ dominates the lattice to maintain a near-ideal Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), thereby minimizing octahedral tilting and lattice strain; this compositional design concurrently suppresses halide vacancy formation and iodide migration, particularly under thermal stress, while the precisely tuned precursor concentration (1.55 mol/L) ensures optimal supersaturation for nucleation control during spin-coating—first at 1000 rpm for 10 s to establish uniform wet-film coverage, then ramped to 5000 rpm for 40 s to drive solvent evaporation and promote oriented crystal growth—where the timed antisolvent quenching with 160 µL chlorobenzene at the critical 10 s mark arrests intermediate solvate phase evolution (e.g., PbI₂·DMSO or FAI–PbI₂ adducts) before irreversible aggregation, enabling homogeneous nucleation across the substrate and suppressing pinhole formation and interfacial voids; subsequent thermal annealing at 120 °C for 13 min facilitates complete ligand expulsion, full crystallization into the photoactive α-phase, and stress relaxation—evidenced by XRD showing no residual PbI₂ peak at ~12.6°, sharp (110) reflection with narrow FWHM (<0.12°), and absence of 2D δ-phase signatures—while optical PL mapping reveals uniformly high and spatially homogeneous photoluminescence intensity with minimal dark spots, confirming nanoscale continuity and suppressed non-radiative recombination centers, and grayscale analysis of top-down SEM/AFM-derived film images quantifies >99.2% surface coverage with RMS roughness <7.3 nm, directly correlating with reduced shunt pathways and enhanced lateral carrier transport; collectively, these morphological, structural, and optical signatures corroborate that the crystallization protocol yields large, strain-relieved grains with low intra-grain defect density and coherent grain boundaries, thereby maximizing carrier diffusion length and minimizing trap-assisted recombination at both bulk and interface—ultimately delivering a certified PCE of 19.5454% with VOC = 1.096 V, JSC = 25.503 mA/cm², and FF = 69.9301%.
